transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Late afternoon settles over the crossroads, where the King’s Road meets a track between tall blackthorn hedges. A dead ox lies in the ditch, arrows jutting from its flank. Crows pick at the air above it; somewhere, woodsmoke rides the wind.

A mud-caked farmer jabs his pitchfork at the hedge, then whirls to shout at the weathered milestone. He looks past fifty and utterly sleepless. “No, you don’t tell me I’m daft, stone! I saw ’em. Little green devils, the lot!” Then he spots you. The pitchfork swings your way. “You! Keep back! I know what you are!”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I stop where I am and slowly lower my travelling pack to the road, palms open, letting him see the sheaf-and-sickle embroidered on my grey robe. "Peace, friend. Peace. I am only Maren, a Sister of the Harvest Mother, on my way to Caerwyn." I glance at the ox in the ditch, then back at his face, softly. "You have not slept, have you? Whatever you saw, it frightened you badly. Tell me what happened here. I will not call you daft."

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Persuasion check: 5 + 3 = 8 vs DC 10: failure

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Tam’s eyes flick to the sheaf-and-sickle, then narrow. “Harvest Mother? Aye, and I’m the king’s own turnip!” He backs away, pitchfork leveled at your chest. “You’re in on it. All of you. They wear skins, don’t they?”

Behind him, the blackthorn hedge rustles once—then goes still. Tam jerks around with a strangled laugh, gripping the pitchfork so hard his knuckles pale. “There! Heard that? They’re watching. They killed my ox, and now they’re after me!”

A crude arrow suddenly thunks into the milestone beside his head. Tam flinches and ducks. “Down, you fools!”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I drop low and scramble to Tam, grabbing his sleeve to pull him down behind the milestone with me. "Stay down, Tam. I have you." Then, without standing, I raise my empty hand above the stone and call toward the hedge, steady and unhurried: "Little ones in the thorns! I am a Sister of the Harvest Mother. I carry no blade. If you are hungry, I have bread and dried apples in my pack, and you may have them. Nobody else needs to bleed today. Come and talk with me."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
You pull Tam down behind the milestone. He makes a small, startled noise, but stays crouched, pitchfork clutched tight.

At your call, five goblins rise among the thorns, short bows trained on the road. Their leader wears a wolf-skin hood strung with teeth; one ear is missing. A bone rattle clicks in his fist.

“Bread?” he shrills. “Skrag wants no bread, longleg! Skrag wants Grandmother Bone—the dirt-scratcher has it!” His knife points toward Tam. “Give back shrine-bone, and Skrag takes his little green devils away.”

Behind you, Tam whispers, “It’s mine. I dug it up fair.” His eyes dart from the bows to you. “You don’t believe him, do you?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I keep my hand on Tam's shoulder and look at him properly for the first time, and something in my face softens with recognition. "Tam... Tam of Hollowmere? You are, aren't you. I blessed the barley at Hollowmere three autumns ago, the year of the rust-blight. Your wife Bess brought honey cakes to the shrine and you carried the last sheaf yourself." I squeeze his shoulder. "I believe you dug it up, Tam. I do. But the Mother teaches that what lies in a grave belongs to the dead and their kin, not to the plough that finds it. Where did you dig it? What is this Grandmother Bone?"

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Tam stares at you, startled by the recognition. “Hollowmere? No—Hollis Farm, down Nine Furrows. Bet’s my wife.” His grip loosens a fraction. “And I didn’t rob any grave. Plough snagged a leather bundle three days back. Inside was a little bone granny with red stones for eyes. I thought to sell it in Caerwyn.”

Skrag clicks his rattle sharply. “Grandmother Bone! Shrine-grandmother. Give her back, longleg!”

Tam presses a hand to his smock, protective. “I dug her up fair.” His voice falters as he glances at the bows. “But… if she’s theirs…” He looks to you, uncertain, while Skrag’s goblins keep their aim trained over the milestone.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I nod slowly. "Hollis Farm. Forgive me, Tam, the years blur. Bet, of course." I lay my hand over his on his smock. "She would want you home tonight more than she would want coin." Then I rise just enough to show my face over the milestone, keeping my hands open, and speak to the one-eared goblin as I would to a grieving widow. "Skrag. Is she your kin? Your grandmother in truth, or your people's mother from long ago? How did she come to be sleeping under a farmer's field?" I pause, gentler still. "And what happens to your people while she is gone? What are you afraid of?"

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Skrag’s grin falters at your gentleness. The bone rattle slows in his fist.

“Not blood-kin,” he says, with a wounded sort of pride. “Grandmother to warren. She watches the dead, keeps the old names. Longlegs dig where they shouldn’t; dirt-scratcher took her from under old mill hill.” His eyes flick toward Tam. “Chieftain says Skrag brings her home, or Skrag loses other ear.”

One goblin snickers, then stops when Skrag glares. His bow remains trained on the milestone, but his knife dips. “You understand, harvest-sister. Skrag wants no dead longlegs. Give Grandmother Bone back. Maybe… bread too.” He glances at Tam’s smock. “Will dirt-scratcher give?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I sink back down beside Tam and speak low, just for him. "Tam, you heard him. She keeps the names of their dead, the way our shrine keeps the harvest rolls. You did not steal her, you found her, and there is no sin in finding. But keeping her now would be." I hold out my cupped hands. "Give her to me. And I swear to you by the Mother's sickle: when I reach Caerwyn, I will stand before the Assembly and see that the temple lends Hollis Farm a plough-ox before the spring furrows. You will not lose your season over this. Will you trust me?"

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Tam’s hand tightens beneath yours. For a moment, he looks ready to argue—then his eyes flick to the bows and the arrow embedded in the milestone.

“Bet’ll skin me if I come home without my hide,” he mutters. “But she’d sooner I came home without a bone doll.” He draws the wrapped idol from his smock and places it in your cupped hands. “Tell the Assembly I’ll remember this, Sister.”

Skrag watches the bundle, wary. “Grandmother Bone,” he says. “Now, longleg. Give her to Skrag—and the bread, if you promised.” The goblins hold their bows, waiting.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I touch Tam's cheek briefly, "The Mother saw that, Tam," then stand and step out from behind the milestone into the open road, the bundle held against my breast like a sleeping child. I set my bread and the pouch of dried apples down on the road between us, then kneel beside them. "The bread is yours, Skrag, freely given." But I do not hold out the bundle. "She is not a sack of turnips to be passed hand to hand at a crossroads. Let me carry her home with you, to your warren, and say the words of returning over her. And let me stand before your Chieftain and tell him Skrag brought her back with no blood spilled. No one should lose an ear for that." I lift my chin toward the wind. "Is that your warren's woodsmoke I smell?"

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The scent of woodsmoke comes stronger on the breeze. Skrag’s eyes flick toward the bread and apples, then settle on the bundle against your breast. His goblins keep their bows trained, but none steps forward.

“Smoke from river, burnt mill,” he says. “Warren below. Skrag takes Grandmother home. No longleg comes to Chieftain’s hall.” He bares his teeth, trying to make the refusal sound like a threat. “Bread is good. But you give bone first.”

Behind you, Tam stays silent. Skrag’s rattle clicks once. “So? You walk with Skrag, or you hand her over?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I rise with the bundle still cradled. "Then I will walk with you, Skrag, to the edge of your warren and not one step past it. I will not shame you before your Chieftain. You will carry her the last of the way yourself, and I will say the words of returning from outside." I look back over my shoulder. "Tam, go home to Bet. Take the road, not the hedges. I will find you at Hollis Farm on my way back from Caerwyn, I promise." Then to Skrag, as we set off, troubled: "A burnt mill, you said. Who burned it? Was anyone hurt?"

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Skrag’s goblins fall in around you, bows still ready, and Tam hurries down the drovers’ track without looking back.

At your question, Skrag gives a sharp, uneasy laugh. “Mill burned before Skrag had teeth. Longlegs did it. No one lives there now—only smoke when the river wind blows.” He reaches for the bread, but keeps his eyes on Grandmother Bone. “You say words here, then give her. No Chieftain. No longleg inside.”

His fingers hover over the loaf. “Or Skrag takes her now.” The goblins shift in the thorns, waiting to see whether you’ll yield.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I stop walking. "Here, then. I will not make you choose between me and your Chieftain." I kneel in the road, take a pinch of seed-barley from the pouch at my belt and scatter it in a ring, and lay the bundle in the middle. But I frown into the wind before I begin. "Skrag. You said the mill burned before you had teeth, and no one lives there. Then whose fire is that? Smoke does not rise from old ashes, not for years. Someone is down by the river now." I look up at him. "Could they be the ones who dug where they should not? Is your warren safe?"

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Skrag’s eyes narrow at your warning. “Wind carries old mill-smoke,” he says, but the answer comes too quickly. He glances north, toward the river, then snaps his gaze back to the idol. “Warren safe. Skrag knows.”

He points his knife at the seed-barley ring. “Words done. Grandmother Bone comes with Skrag. Now.”

One of the goblins nocks an arrow. Skrag holds up three fingers and begins counting down, badly: “Three… two…” His hand tightens around the rattle. The bread and apples lie untouched between you.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I do not flinch at the counting. I lift the bundle from the barley ring and hold it out to him in both hands, bowing my head. "Mother of the furrow, who keeps all that is planted and all that is laid to rest: this one was taken from her sleep. We return her now to those who love her. Let the names she keeps be kept." I place her in Skrag's hands and let my fingers linger on his for a moment. "There. She is home with you, and no one bled." Then, quieter, only to him: "You answered too fast about the smoke, Skrag. If something by the river frightens your warren, you can come to me. I mean that."

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Skrag takes Grandmother Bone in both hands. At your quiet warning, his eyes meet yours; the bravado slips for a heartbeat.

“Smoke is smoke,” he mutters. “Skrag will look.” He tucks the idol close beneath his wolf-skin hood, then snatches up the bread and apples. “No blood spilled. Good.” His goblins lower their bows and melt back into the blackthorn, following him toward the river.

The crossroads falls quiet except for the crows and the wind. Tam is already on the road home. Your pack lies where you set it down, and Caerwyn waits along the King’s Road.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text: Skrag cradles Grandmother Bone beneath his wolf-skin hood and gives you a stiff, solemn nod. “No blood spilled,” he says, as though he had planned it all along; then he and his goblins melt into the hedges, leaving the bread and apples untouched. Far down the track, Tam pauses and looks back, one hand pressed to his empty smock. “Bet’s going to ask where the coin went,” he calls, before turning toward home.

transcript.speaker: system
transcript.text: Scene ends: Grandmother Bone goes home
